html:
Papillon is a memoir by Henri Charrière, published in 1969, about his years in the penal colony of French Guiana and his escapes. It sold millions of copies and was made into a film in 1973.

Charrière was convicted of murder in Paris in 1931, a crime he always denied, and sent to French Guiana in 1933. He tells of breakouts by boat, life among the convicts, time on the Îles du Salut, and his final escape to Venezuela, where he settled.

Critics later showed that he took many stories from other prisoners and made himself the hero. Still, the book brought the horror of the bagne, the French penal system, to a world audience. The prison buildings at Saint-Laurent-du-Maroni, near the border with Suriname, are now a museum.
sum: Papillon is a memoir by Henri Charrière, published in 1969, about his years in the penal colony of French Guiana and his escapes. It sold millions of copies and was made into a film in 1973.
